chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He was asked about a man who was entrusted with camels and sent with oil to a land, and he claimed that some of the oil skins had burst, so he spilled what was in them. He said: 'If he wishes, he may take the oil.' And he said: 'He claimed it burst, but he is not believed except with a just witness.'

key_terms.أَزْقَاق: skins or bags for holding oil
key_terms.أُسْتُكْرِيَ: was entrusted / was given a trust

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a trustee claiming loss of entrusted goods due to broken containers?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the evidentiary standard for trustees claiming partial loss of entrusted goods, ruling that mere assertion is insufficient without a just witness (*bayyinah adil*). This highlights the Shia legal principle that the burden of proof lies with the trustee to validate their claim of loss, ensuring fairness in commercial transactions and preventing unjust enrichment.
